_comment: The golden set for plan 30 §5 — real topo photos with a hand-checked expected outcome
each, run deliberately (never in CI) before and after a prompt change. Checked in empty
on purpose, for the same reason GoldenSet.json is: the entries have to be verified by a
human against the actual image, and inventing them would measure nothing.
Unlike the enrichment set, the inputs here are images, and images are not checked into
this repository (it is public, and these are third-party scans — see plan 30 §5). Each
entry names a blob in the topos container instead, and the harness downloads it:
blobName:  a blob in the 'topos' container, e.g. '_goldenset/guidebook-01.jpg'
isTopo:    what the gate should answer
areaBreadcrumb: the sector the uploader would have picked, passed to the extraction
expectedName / expectedGrade: what a correct extraction reads off the image, or null
when the correct answer is to discard (unnamed panel, several routes,
unreadable print). A discard where a discard is right counts as a hit —
precision is the target, as in plan 29.
Fill it with a dozen images spanning the hard cases: a clean guidebook page, a weathered
panel photo, a phone snap at an angle, a topo showing several routes, a page whose grade
is UIAA rather than French, and two or three non-topos (a landscape, a selfie, a
screenshot). Then run:
dotnet test backend/Acordanza.Worker.Tests --filter "Category=Enrichment"
with Anthropic:FoundryResource and Storage:* configured, and an az login session holding
Cognitive Services User on the Foundry resource plus Storage Blob Data Reader on the
account. A pass is cheap by design — about $0.05 an entry, so under a dollar for a full
set, against roughly $15 for the enrichment one.
Both CI test jobs exclude Category=Enrichment (.github/workflows/ci-cd.yml), which is
what keeps this from ever running on a push.
